hypothesis: In a database of naturalised plants, European-native species naturalised in the La Plata region and in Australia far outnumber southern-hemisphere-native species naturalised anywhere in Europe, and the La Plata excess is larger than the Australian one.
pass_criterion: Using GloNAF region-level naturalisation lists joined to native-range data, let A_LP be the number of taxa native to Europe that are naturalised in the La Plata region (Buenos Aires province, Argentina, plus Uruguay). Let A_AU be the same count for Australia. Let B be the number of taxa native only to the southern hemisphere (native range wholly south of the equator) that are naturalised in at least one European region. The claim is confirmed if A_LP/B >= 10 AND A_AU/B >= 10 AND B is under 5% of all taxa naturalised in Europe AND A_LP is greater than A_AU. The last condition is the 'lesser degree in Australia' clause. It is checked as the number of European-origin naturalised taxa per unit of recorded native flora in each region, if native flora sizes are available. Otherwise raw counts are used.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if either A_LP/B < 3 or A_AU/B < 3, or if B is at least 15% of Europe's naturalised taxa. It is also refuted if the Australian European-origin count exceeds the La Plata count by more than 25% on both the raw and the per-native-flora measures. Results between these bounds are reported as inconclusive.
interpretation: Darwin's 'European productions' that 'cover the ground' and 'beat the natives' are read as taxa native to Europe that are recorded as naturalised, meaning self-sustaining populations, in the target region. His 'southern forms' are read as taxa with native ranges wholly in the southern hemisphere. 'Naturalised in any part of Europe' is read as GloNAF records for European regions. 'Partly displaced the natives' cannot be measured from presence lists, so the test covers only the naturalisation asymmetry. The modern reinterpretation is that the analysis is limited to vascular plants, because GloNAF records only plants, although Darwin's 'productions' also include animals. La Plata is operationalised as Buenos Aires province plus Uruguay. The test counts species, not abundance or cover. The native-range assignment would use the native-distribution fields supplied with GloNAF, or a join to the WCVP/POWO native ranges by taxon name.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF)
dataset.publisher: GloNAF consortium (van Kleunen, Pyšek, Dawson, Essl and others), hosted at glonaf.org
dataset.why_it_fits: GloNAF records which vascular plant taxa are naturalised in more than 1000 regions worldwide, including Argentine provinces, Uruguay, Australian states and European countries. Fields to use: taxon name (standardised), region and country, and the status and native-range attributes. Counting naturalised taxa per region and cross-tabulating by native origin gives the north-to-south versus south-to-north counts directly.
